title: Llama-Mobile: A VLM at 2.7 Bits per Weight
hook: Llama 3.2 11B Vision squeezed into 3.7 GB — using the model's own outputs as calibration data and a bit format built for Arm CPUs, not GPUs.
key_points: Vision-language models are hard to deploy on phones: memory and compute both blow the budget.
The pipeline uses the model itself to generate its quantization training data — no access to the original training setup needed.
A novel 2.7-bit-per-parameter format is designed for efficient execution on Arm CPUs.
Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct compresses to 3.7 GB with 8-bit activations.
The authors report strong retained performance on standard visual question answering tasks.
content_html: Getting a vision-language model onto a phone is mostly a memory problem, and the usual answer is aggressive weight quantization. Luka Ribar, Jeevan Bhoot and Douglas Orr present a framework that pairs two pieces: a quantization pipeline that bootstraps its own calibration data from the model being compressed — so no access to the original training setup is required — and a 2.7-bit-per-parameter number format chosen for what Arm CPUs can actually execute quickly.
extra_html: Applied to Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct, the combination lands the model at 3.7 GB with 8-bit activations, which the authors report preserves strong performance across a set of standard visual question answering tasks. The interesting angle is the hardware-first framing: most low-bit research optimizes for accuracy at a bit width and assumes GPU kernels, while here the format itself is shaped by the deployment target. Details on arXiv.

related.title: KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian
related.hook: GPTQ assumes every output channel matters equally. KronQ adds gradient information to challenge that — rescuing 2-bit LLaMA-3-70B from a perplexity blowup down to 7.93.

related.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Why 'Same Accuracy' Doesn't Mean 'Same Model'
related.hook: Two quantized models can score identically on accuracy while disagreeing on which individual examples they get right — a gap standard benchmarks are structurally blind to.

flashcards.prompt: Why does using the model's own generations as calibration data matter practically?
flashcards.back_html: It removes the need for access to the original training data or training setup — anyone with the weights can run the quantization pipeline.

flashcards.prompt: What is unusual about the 2.7-bit format in Llama-Mobile?

choices.text: It's designed for efficient execution on Arm CPUs rather than GPU kernels
It uses a different bit width per layer chosen by search
It quantizes activations to 2.7 bits as well as weights

flashcards.explanation_html: The target is on-device mobile inference, so the format is built around what Arm CPUs can execute efficiently; activations stay at 8 bits.
